elements.scope_reason: Red-box criterion with eight parts: infection (surrounding skin red/warm/swollen), SBP < 80, pulse > 100, temperature >= 38, confused, blisters, crepitus, severe pain.
elements.problem: All eight parts are present with the right logic: infection AND any-of the seven signs, inside the Urgent rule. Infection is modelled as (or Infected ulcer of skin / Local infection of wound); the page's parenthetical (red/warm/swollen) is a definition, not a separate criterion, so folding it into one infection finding is acceptable. Thresholds and directions are right (< 80 mmHg, > 100 bpm, >= 38 °C). Two caveats lower my confidence slightly: (1) pulse uses the observable 'Pulse, function'; 'Heart rate' (observable entity) also exists and I cannot verify which one VHA records as the routine vital, so if it is the wrong one the pulse criterion silently never fires; (2) 'Severe pain' is unsited, so any severe pain recorded anywhere satisfies this part, a small over-trigger.

elements.scope_reason: Red-box criterion naming a likely diagnosis: muscle pain in legs/buttocks on exercise (claudication) AND (pain at rest OR gangrene) -> critical limb ischaemia likely -> urgent.
elements.problem: Encoded as the house pattern: a probable diagnosis rule (claudication AND (rest pain OR gangrene)) and a priority rule referencing (active_condition Critical lower limb ischemia). 'Intermittent claudication' covers 'muscle pain in legs or buttocks on exercise'. 'Pain provoked by rest' is the SNOMED finding whose synonym is 'rest pain'; it is the best unqualified concept available ('Pain at rest due to peripheral vascular disease' presupposes the diagnosis). 'Gangrenous disorder' is a reasonable general parent. All three findings are in the check list.

elements.scope_reason: Flowchart decision: 'Is ulcer on the lower leg or foot?' gates the arterial, venous and diabetic branches.
parts_missing: Ankle: 'Ankle region structure' is not a descendant of 'Foot structure' or of 'Structure of lower limb from knee to ankle' (its parents are 'Structure of ankle and/or foot' and 'Structure of joint region of lower limb'), so an ulcer recorded at the ankle, a site the check list itself offers, does not satisfy this clause in any of the three rules.
elements.problem: The clause is encoded as (or ulcer@knee-to-ankle ulcer@foot), which is the right reading of 'lower leg or foot', but the ankle, the classic site of venous ulcers and listed as a pressure site in the same file, falls between the two SNOMED structures. A non-bedridden patient whose ulcer is recorded at 'Ankle region structure' gets no arterial, venous or diabetic diagnosis. Adding ulcer@Ankle region structure (or using 'Structure of ankle and/or foot' in place of 'Foot structure') to the disjunction would close the gap. Heel is fine: 'Heel structure' is a descendant of 'Foot structure'.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable arterial (ischaemic) ulcer / venous ulcer / diabetic ulcer (APC 2026 page 90)
rule_level_problems.problem: The 'lower leg or foot' clause is (or ulcer@'Structure of lower limb from knee to ankle' ulcer@'Foot structure'). 'Ankle region structure' is a descendant of neither (SNOMED parents: 'Structure of ankle and/or foot', 'Structure of joint region of lower limb'), yet the same file's check list offers ulcer@Ankle region structure as a recordable site. A non-bedridden patient whose ulcer is recorded at the ankle, the commonest venous ulcer site, satisfies none of the three rules. Add ulcer@Ankle region structure to the disjunction (and to the check list it already is) or replace 'Foot structure' with 'Structure of ankle and/or foot'.

If VHA records the routine pulse vital under a different concept, the 'pulse > 100' criterion never fires. Needs confirming against the vital's recorded concept.

'Buttock structure' and 'Ischial tuberosity structure' exist and could be added so a buttock ulcer in a wheelchair user is a pressure ulcer. The figure is the only source for the site list, so this is a judgment call.

rule_level_problems.problem: Infection is (or 'Infected ulcer of skin' 'Local infection of wound'). 'Cellulitis' and 'Wound cellulitis' are not descendants of either, so an infected ulcer recorded as cellulitis (the clinical name for 'surrounding skin red/warm/swollen') does not trigger the Urgent rule unless the nurse also picks one of the two listed findings. Low because the check list steers the nurse to the listed concepts.

rule_level_problems.problem: 'Severe pain' is unsited, so severe pain recorded for any reason (e.g. a headache) plus an infected ulcer satisfies the rule. Over-triggering, not under-triggering, and the page's wording is equally unsited, so low.

summary: The red box and all four flowchart diagnoses are encoded with the right concepts, thresholds and branch logic, and every check_for item is consumed by a rule. The one substantive gap is that 'Ankle region structure' is not under 'Foot structure' or the knee-to-ankle structure in SNOMED, so an ulcer recorded at the ankle (which the check list itself offers) can never reach the arterial, venous or diabetic rules. The pulse observable ('Pulse, function' rather than 'Heart rate') should be confirmed against the concept VHA records for the routine vital; the pressure-site list could add buttock/ischial sites for wheelchair users.
